message.reasoning:
With a shortfall of 9, I'm weighing options: mortgaging B&O gives $100 but keeps the houses, while selling one house gives $50 but cuts rent income and risks breaking even-building rules. Mortgaging B&O would also cost railroad rent, though I need to check how rent scales with the number of railroads owned versus mortgaged.

Comparing losses, selling a house off St. Charles drops rent from $625 to $450—a $175 hit—while mortgaging B&O sacrifices roughly $200 in potential rent, so they're in the same ballpark, but mortgaging gives more cash and is cheaper to reverse later. Since my opponents are already low on cash, high rents don't matter as much anyway, so I'll mortgage B&O instead of selling a house.
